children: Australia's economy lost momentum in the second quarter as higher borrowing costs and costly fuel squeezed households, though growth remained solid enough to keep a near-term interest rate hike firmly in play.

Markets responded by boosting the odds of a fourth rate hike from the Reserve Bank of Australia at its September policy meeting to 57%, from 48% before. A move by November has been more than fully priced in. (0#AUDIRPR)
Data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics on Wednesday showed real gross domestic product (GDP) rose a moderate 0.4% in the second quarter, just above market forecasts of a 0.3% gain.
Annual growth dropped to 2.1%, from 2.5%, but topped forecasts of 1.8%. That was still above the 2% speed limit the RBA believes can be sustained without generating inflation.

"The Middle East conflict influenced spending behaviour with falls in fuel consumption in response to elevated prices, and reduced domestic and international travel," said Grace Kim, ABS head of National Accounts.
However, purchases of vehicles, mostly of EVs, jumped 10% in the quarter, which contributed 0.3 percentage points to GDP growth.

The economy is cooling as expected but inflation is still running hot. Consumer inflation eased to 3.5% in July but the trimmed mean measure remained stubborn at 3.6%, with both well above the central bank's target band of 2% to 3%.
For the quarter, business investment fell 0.5% after a surge in the first quarter as companies poured into data center machinery and equipment.

Net exports added 0.1 percentage point to growth, while public demand also contributed a meagre 0.1 percentage point. Household consumption added 0.2 percentage points, driven mostly by the purchase of EVs.
